chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Sufyan ibn al-Simpt, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: "When you enter from the second door on the right side of the mosque, counting five pillars, two of them are in the shade and three of them are in the courtyard; then at the third one is the Musalla of Ibrahim (peace be upon him), and it is the fifth from the wall."

He said: So when it was the days of Abu al-Abbas, Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) entered from the Bab al-Fil (Door of the Elephant) and moved along the wall upon entering from the door, and prayed near the fourth pillar, which is opposite the fifth. I said to him: 'That pillar is the Musalla of Ibrahim (peace be upon him).' He said to me: 'Yes.'

key_terms.أَبُو الْعَبَّاسِ: Abu al- Abbas (referring to Caliph al-Saffah or al-Mansur)
key_terms.مُصَلَّى إِبْرَاهِيمَ: Musalla of Ibrahim (the prayer station of Prophet Ibrahim)

ai.seo_question: Where is the Musalla of Ibrahim located in the Grand Mosque according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith provides precise architectural markers for the Musalla of Ibrahim within the Grand Mosque, linking the physical space to the legacy of Prophet Ibrahim. Imam al-Sadiq’s personal verification by praying at the fourth pillar during the Abbasid era underscores the authenticity of this location and highlights the Imams' role in preserving the sanctity of Islamic sites against political changes.
